entrypoints.summary: The /dev/vpu driver is visible to the mediacodec SELinux context and exposes the Wave677DV hardware interface, including an mmap path for MMIO registers.

affected_components.file: Pixel Wave677DV VPU driver source (path not supplied)
affected_components.role: Maps the VPU physical base using caller-controlled VMA length rather than a bounded MMIO aperture.

code_slices.surrounding_context: The handler marks the VMA as I/O, selects device page protection, and is intended to map VPU control/status registers; no source path or fixed implementation is provided.
code_slices.vulnerable: vpu_mmap computes pfn = core->paddr >> PAGE_SHIFT and passes vm->vm_end - vm->vm_start as the remap_pfn_range length.

capabilities.concept: oversized physical-memory mapping from VPU MMIO base

impacts.concept: mediacodec sandbox escape through kernel code execution

relation_candidates.dst: oversized physical-memory mapping from VPU MMIO base
relation_candidates.rationale: The exposed mmap handler uses the requested VMA size without bounding it to the VPU register aperture.
The reported mapping extends from the VPU physical base into the higher-addressed kernel image, which the writeup says can be accessed and modified.

relation_candidates.rationale: The writeup states that modifying the mapped kernel image by overwriting a kernel function yields kernel code execution.

relation_candidates.dst: mediacodec sandbox escape through kernel code execution
relation_candidates.rationale: The post presents the /dev/vpu flaw as the local privilege-escalation link reachable from the mediacodec context and states that overwriting a kernel function yields kernel code execution.

Limiting a mapping to the VPU register-region extent prevents oversized mappings from extending into adjacent physical memory. This is the invariant implied by the reported root cause, not a verified description of the vendor patch.

impact.affected_asset: Pixel kernel image (.text and .data) located above the VPU register physical address.
impact.attacker_capability: A caller with access to /dev/vpu can request an oversized mapping and directly read or write reachable kernel physical memory; in the described chain this provides an escape from mediacodec confinement.
impact.security_effect: Kernel physical-memory access beyond the VPU MMIO aperture, including modification of kernel text and data and documented kernel code execution.

causal_trace.summary: A caller able to access /dev/vpu requests an mmap with a chosen VMA size; the post identifies the device as visible from the mediacodec SELinux context.
vpu_mmap is intended to map the bounded VPU MMIO register physical-address region, but it does not constrain requested VMA length to that register-region extent.
vpu_mmap derives a PFN from core->paddr and invokes remap_pfn_range with vm_end - vm_start as the length, allowing an oversized mapping beginning at the VPU physical base.

The oversized mapping can reach higher physical addresses containing the Pixel kernel image, allowing userspace access to and modification of kernel .text and .data; the post states that overwriting a kernel function yields kernel code execution.

failure.operation: remap_pfn_range(vm, vm->vm_start, core->paddr >> PAGE_SHIFT, vm->vm_end - vm->vm_start, vm->vm_page_prot)

primary_invariant.statement: A VPU mmap request must map no more than the physical extent of the VPU MMIO register region beginning at core->paddr.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The handler supplies the caller-selected VMA size to remap_pfn_range without bounding it to the MMIO register-region size.

provenance.source_id: Project Zero Pixel 10 VPU mmap case study (2026-05-13)

quality.review_notes: The primary public writeup supplies the vulnerable handler and directly describes the mapping consequence and kernel-code-execution outcome. It reports an exploit requiring five lines for kernel arbitrary read/write, but the bundle contains no executable reproducer, test, runtime trace, fixed driver diff, resolved VPU identifier, or VPU-specific bulletin row; no execution result is asserted here. The Google Messages/Dolby material supports general chain-entrypoint context, but is not treated as byte-identical proof of the Pixel 10 first stage.

remediation.invariant_restored: The actual fixed diff is unavailable. A remediation must ensure the remapped length cannot exceed the VPU MMIO register region; the primary post only confirms a February 2026 Pixel-bulletin patch, not its implementation.
mitigation_classes: Bound VMA mapping length to the device MMIO register aperture
Restrict direct user mapping of hardware MMIO

state_context.attacker_state_setup: The caller needs access to /dev/vpu. The primary writeup states that this device is visible from the mediacodec SELinux context.
data_structure_invariants: core->paddr identifies the start of the VPU MMIO register region.
The requested VMA extent must not exceed the physical VPU register-region extent.

numeric_domains.attacker_constraints: The caller chooses mmap size; the post states that requesting a size larger than the register region produces the overbroad mapping.
numeric_domains.name: VMA mapping length

state_context.state_machine: A mediacodec-context process accesses /dev/vpu and requests its MMIO mmap; the handler turns the VMA length into a physical mapping length.
